title: fix(console): route the Studio landing's wordmark tooltip through i18n
body:
Fixes #10043

Clause-②: no — a user-visible string routed through the app's existing i18n. It moves no exported symbol and no key on a published payload.

## Premise, re-taken before any edit

The card read `title="..."` as a Chinese literal at line 108 on `0febe1a59`. On today's `origin/main` `0c2eb5eee` the line number has moved to 121 and **the string is still there** — the string was the anchor, not the address.

The card's own control was carried, and it has drifted: the card recorded `title=` matches in **4** files under `apps/console/src`; the same instrument on `0c2eb5eee` reports **14**. The finding is unaffected (the reader finds those files and finds this one), but the card's figure is a number written into prose that was derived once — commandment #9's own failure mode, so it is reported rather than repeated.

## The i18n mechanism this follows, and why it is the one this surface uses

The repair routes the tooltip through **`useObjectTranslation` from `@object-ui/i18n`, with the key in the `console.*` bundle** — `console.studio.backToHome`, added to all ten locale packs.

That mechanism was chosen over the alternative by what is actually reachable here, not by preference:

- **It is what the surrounding surface uses.** `useObjectTranslation` is the translator in 38 files under `apps/console/src`; the provider is mounted above this component in `main.tsx`, so the hook resolves at this call site with nothing new wired.
- **The repo has already ruled on this exact defect shape, in this exact namespace.** The `console.settingsView.*` block carries a comment recording objectui#4024: that screen's chrome "was a hardcoded English literal while its sibling resolved through the bundle", and the ruling was to key it into `console.*`. This card is the same defect one namespace over.
- **The sibling screen's mechanism is NOT reachable from here.** `StudioDesignSurface` resolves the identical affordance through app-shell's metadata-admin catalogue (`engine.studio.home`, which already reads "Back to home"). But `@object-ui/app-shell` publishes only its `.` entry, and that barrel does not export that `t` or `useMetadataLocale`. Using it would mean widening a package's public surface — a larger change than this card describes, so it was not taken.

⚠️ A raw English literal was explicitly **not** the repair. It satisfies the letter of commandment #-1 and leaves the surface untranslatable, which is the worse outcome for an international project — the card's scope note says so and it is right.

**Translation, not transliteration, and not invented.** Every one of the ten values is this repo's own existing wording for the English string "Back to home" — the value each pack already carries on its `empty.appAccessDeniedHome` entry. So the new key speaks each pack's established word for this affordance instead of introducing a second spelling of it. ⚠️ One consequence worth naming: the Chinese value is now the pack's existing term rather than the exact characters removed. The two are synonyms; the pack's own consistency was preferred, and that choice is reversible in one line if a maintainer disagrees.

## First half — the `title` attribute. RED before, GREEN after.

New pin: `apps/console/src/components/StudioRoute.landingI18n.test.tsx`. It drives the real `studioRoutes` tree and mocks `t` to answer in key sentinels, the technique `AppManagementPage.i18n.test.tsx` documents — an echo-the-default mock cannot tell a hardcoded literal from a correct lookup.

**RED, before the source change** (4 tests: 2 failed, 2 passed):

- the key sentinel is absent from the DOM;
- the Han sweep over attribute values fails, printing the literal it found;
- **and the two control assertions passed** — the sweep regex matches a Han code point and does not match "Back to home". That is what makes the later zero a reading rather than a dark instrument.

**GREEN, after** — the new file plus the pre-existing `StudioRoute.test.tsx`, run together: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 21 passed (21)`.

The sweep checks attribute values separately from `textContent`, because `textContent` never sees an attribute and the measured defect **was** an attribute. The Han sample is built with `String.fromCodePoint` rather than written out, so the file enforcing the commandment does not itself violate it.

## Second half — the Chinese source comments. The card declared this UNMEASURED; it is now measured.

**⚠️ The first instrument was dark, and the control caught it.** `grep -P '\p{Han}'` reported **0** on the subject — and also **0** on a file that provably contains Han (the app-shell catalogue). This container's GNU grep does not honour that property class. Reporting "absent" from that probe would have been exactly the error the dispatch warns about.

Re-measured with a working probe, subject and control in the same command:

| | Han-bearing lines |
|---|---|
| `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, before | 30 |
| `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, after | 0 |
| control (`metadata-admin/i18n.ts`), same command, after | 2009 |

The control still reads 2009 in the same run that reads 0 on the subject, so the zero is a reading.

All 30 were comments (line, block, JSDoc and JSX), every one of them referencing a UI label in Chinese. They are rewritten to the label's **own English**, read off `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` rather than translated freehand — "Save draft", "More", "Open app", "Create app", "Advanced", "Records / Form", "Add field", "New object", "Publish", "Loading…".

**Comments only, proved mechanically rather than by eye.** Both revisions were emitted with `removeComments: true` and hashed: **byte-identical, 125428 bytes, same sha256**. The instrument carries its own control — the same comparison on a copy with a single identifier renamed reports DIFFERENT. ⛔ No code, no behaviour, no string literal moved.

## The extra question triage asked — answered, ⛔ not acted on

> **The fix is one attribute; the question worth one extra minute is whether a gate exists** — a commandment this absolute with no mechanical reader will be violated again.

**Answer: no gate enforces commandment #-1. Nothing in this repo mechanically reads it.** Evidence, by elimination against a probe shown to work:

- **No ESLint rule.** `eslint-rules/` holds 11 rules; none concerns language or script.
- **No workflow.** No workflow under `.github/workflows/` scans for non-English text.
- **`check:control-bytes` is not it.** Its own header scopes it to control characters — a grep-outage class. Letters outside ASCII are not in its set, and it is green on this defect by design.
- **`check:i18n-keys` is blind to it by construction.** It reports a `t()` key no pack defines. A hardcoded literal calls no `t()`, so it has nothing to report — it was green on this very line.
- **What does exist is narrow and per-component**: a handful of assertions in `packages/fields` and `packages/app-shell` pinning that one specific rendered string is not CJK when no provider is mounted, plus locale-pack script assertions in `packages/i18n` asserting values ARE in the pack's script. None generalises past its own component.

The probe used to reach that conclusion finds all of those sites, so the absence of a repo-wide gate is a reading and not a failed search.

⛔ **No gate was built, widened or added here** — a new gate is a maintainer-floor decision and this card did not ask for one. The scale question it turns on is in the acceptance notes below.

## Gates and tests

Everything below ran on the exact tree that was pushed, `d9c8d8c7e`, with `git status --porcelain` empty and nothing unstaged.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 |
| `check:i18n-keys` | exit 0 |
| `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | exit 0 |
| `check:i18n-designer-parity` | exit 0 |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 |
| `check:changeset-presence` | exit 0 |
| `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0 |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `type-check` — i18n, app-shell, console | exit 0 (after building the dependency closure) |
| `lint` — i18n, app-shell, console | exit 0 |
| `vitest run packages/i18n/` | 69 files, 1145 tests passed |
| `vitest run apps/console/` | 104 files, 1177 tests passed |

**Two of those greens were checked for vacancy rather than assumed:**

- `check:control-bytes` — its `--list` mode prints only the files it SKIPS (85 binaries). None of the 14 changed paths is in that list, so all of them sit inside the 8118 it scanned.
- `check:i18n-keys` — proved by ablation that it reads the new call site. The key was repointed at one no pack defines; the mutation was verified on disk (injected text present, original absent, blob hash moved off the HEAD blob) and the gate went **red naming this exact call site**: `1 call site references a key the en pack does not define`. Restore was verified by content and hash, ⛔ not by an exit code — on-disk blob back to `49449c46`, injected text gone, `git diff HEAD` empty.

⚠️ **The typecheck greens are only meaningful post-build.** Run against an unbuilt closure all three failed with `TS6305` / "cannot find module" — unbuilt `dist`, not type errors. They were re-run after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' run build` and all three are clean.

**Not measured here:** the repo-wide `pnpm lint` / full `pnpm test` farm, which CI owns.

**Changeset:** decided by running the gate, not from memory. It went red naming 3 released packages, and green once `.changeset/10043-studio-landing-tooltip-i18n.md` declared `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n` as `patch`. ⚠️ `@object-ui/app-shell` is deliberately **not** declared: its only change is comments, which releases nothing — the gate is presence-scoped, and its own header says so.

## Acceptance notes

**To file — same declared contract, outside this card's two files.** A reading taken on `d9c8d8c7e`, over tracked `packages|apps` `**/src/*.ts(x)` minus locale catalogues: **847 files** carry Han outside a catalogue (187 non-test, 660 test). ⚠️ That figure is an **upper bound, not a defect count** — it has not been triaged, and it certainly includes legitimate carriers such as tests asserting Chinese rendering and translation tables the filter did not exclude. It is offered as the scale input for the gate decision triage asked about, not as a work item. Heaviest non-test carriers on this reading: `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`, `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`, `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`. Dedupe words: `english-only commandment` · `Chinese source comments` · `non-ASCII source sweep` · `commandment #-1 gate` · `i18n literal census`.

**Noted, not filed — the card's stale control figure.** 4 then, 14 now, on an instrument that works either way. Carrier: this pull request's premise section, which is where a reader of the card will meet it.

**Noted, not filed — `grep -P '\p{Han}'` is dark in this container.** Not a repo defect; an agent-environment hazard. Carrier: this pull request body, read by whoever measures a script class next.

**Noted, not filed — 16 further files under `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` carry Han comments**, almost all test files. They are inside the directory this card touched but outside the file it named; they are a subset of the 847 above and belong to that card, not a second one.

## What this pull request deliberately does not do

⛔ No label applied. ⛔ Not flipped out of draft. ⛔ No auto-merge. ⛔ No gate built. ⛔ No second issue opened from this seat.
